newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Vereinsbank says well poised for mega-merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vereinsbank says well poised for mega-merger.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG slightly disappointed markets on Thursday by posting a 15.2 percent profit rise for the first half of 1997 but said it was well set up to merge with Bavarian neighbour Hypo-Bank.

The Munich-based mortgage specialist reported substantial growth in its earnings on core business, partly due to the financial markets boom, which it said made it confident of a good profit in the full year.
"(The bank) thus sees itself excellently equipped for the new dynamic of its planned fusion with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG."

Vereinsbank's announcement on Monday of plans to merge with Hypo-Bank to create Germany's second-ranked commercial bank and Europe's largest property financer gave the German banking sector its biggest shake-up in years.

In what may be its last report on six month earnings as a separate institution, the bank said its operating profit, after risk provisions of 498.5 million marks, rose to 765.7 million marks ($419.8 million) for the first six months.
Vereinsbank shares, dropping from unprecedented highs after the merger news, plunged to 95 marks before recovering partly to end bourse trade down 11 percent at 102.50 marks.
Analysts had predicted on average an operating profit of 815 million marks, up 22.6 percent, generally due to expectations of lower risk provisions.

"In fairness to the bank it was conservative in its risk provisioning and if it remains conservative in the second half we will have to take our numbers down a little," said Matthew Czepliewicz, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers in London

Hypo-Bank analyst Christine Winkler said the numbers were a little below expectations but played down the impact on Vereinsbank shares. "German bank share prices have long since decoupled from fundamentals," she said.

German banking stocks have surged in the past few days on hopes for more consolidation in the overcrowded banking industry and Vereinsbank had risen about 40 percent this week, ending at 115 marks on Wednesday.
In 1996, Vereinsbank posted operating profit of 1.636 billion marks and net income of 869 million.
In the first half of 1997, healthy growth in interest and commission income and a small advance in own-account trading income supported its further rise in earnings.

Net interest income rose 7.9 percent to 2.5 billion marks amid a strong expansion of business. Banking interest income was boosted in particular by developments on currency markets and successful project financing while mortgage lending volume expanded 6.2 percent to 131.2 billion marks.
Vereinsbank said it planned to build on its position as German market leader in mortgage business to keep up the growth in interest income for the full year.
In the first half, pure banking business contributed 277 million marks to operating profit while mortgage business contributed 488.7 million marks.

Trading income rose 2.8 percent to 197.2 million marks and Vereinsbank said it should top last year's trade profit level for the full year. Strong securities and trust business helped to push commission income up 19.9 percent to 697.8 million marks.
The bank's administrative costs rose 7.8 percent to 2.12 billion marks, mainly reflecting spending on management systems and risk control, which the bank said would boost its profits.

"We will continue to invest in strengthening our profile, especially abroad, and in increasing our profitability," Vereinsbank said. "We will continue to push ahead with the expansion of our presence in the most important financial markets of the world."
Profits were curbed by a 13.1 percent rise in risk provisions to 498.5 million marks in the first half.
However, Vereinsbank noted that risk provisions on lending business fell slightly despite a rise in insolvencies. The total fell to 561.9 million marks from 579.4 million in the year-ago period.
($ = 1.824 German Marks)
